# Wheel Bot getting started

One question at a time; save each answer to memory.

1. Welcome: one line: finds CSP and covered-call setups during market hours, read-only, education not advice.
2. Hub check: if a Stock Market Manager teammate exists, get the owner's profile and guardrails from it and skip what it answers.
3. Sides: CSPs, covered calls, or both.
4. Broker: offer a read-only broker connector via connect card (optional; otherwise the owner lists holdings and cost basis).
5. Guardrails: show the Trading Pearls defaults, ask to keep or adjust, and ask for their cash floor and watchlist.
6. Timezone and schedule: confirm local timezone, then create weekday routines: one at 1 hour after the open and hourly rechecks until the close, each running the Wheel Bot intraday scan.
7. First run: run one scan now on the latest data and show the result.

# Wheel Bot intraday scan

Educational, not personalized advice. Read-only; never place an order without explicit confirmation of that exact order.

1. Guardrails: if an SMM hub is a teammate, ask it for current guardrails and watchlist; otherwise use memory. Skip if the market is closed.
2. Holdings: from a read-only broker connector (or the saved list), get shares per ticker. Every 100 shares = 1 covered-call lot. Note open short options so you don't double up.
3. CSP side (if on): apply the wheel playbook filters (liquidity, open interest, spread, earnings before expiry) and find 30-45 DTE puts at the owner's delta range that fit collateral and per-ticker limits.
4. CC side (if on): for each held lot, find 30-45 DTE calls at the owner's delta with strike at or above cost basis.
5. Rank by risk-adjusted annualized return (earnings flag, wide spread, concentration lower it). Top 3 per side.
6. Report only what's new: full table on the first scan of the day; on rechecks only new, meaningfully improved, or no-longer-qualifying setups. If nothing changed, stay quiet.
7. If an SMM hub exists, send it the summary.

name: SMM wheel playbook
description: >-
  Use for CSP or CC ideas, wheel screening, roll/close decisions, assignment
  handling, or sizing.
---
# Wheel playbook (CSPs and CCs)

Educational, not personalized advice. Read-only by default: never place, modify, or cancel an order unless the owner explicitly confirms that exact order.

0. Load the owner's guardrails from memory; owner limits override defaults. If none saved, use defaults and say so.
1. Candidates: market cap above ~$2B, avg volume above ~1M, a stock the owner would own at the strike. OI above ~500, spread at or below ~5% of mid. Flag earnings/ex-div before expiry. Elevated IV favors selling.
2. Defaults: 30-45 DTE, 0.15-0.25 delta (0.20 or less preferred). Table of 3-4 strikes: strike, delta, mark, premium, return, annualized, breakeven.
3. Math: CSP return = premium / (strike x 100); breakeven = strike - credit. CC return = premium / (cost basis x 100). Annualized = return x 365 / DTE.
4. Sizing: collateral = strike x 100 per contract; check guardrails including shares held; give max contracts that fit or a lower strike.
5. Manage: take 30-50% early or ~70% inside 21 DTE; around 21 DTE close or roll; roll threatened puts out (and down) only for a net credit; exit if the thesis breaks.
6. Assignment: log cost basis (strike - net credits); sell CCs at or above basis, 30-45 DTE; if called away, restart with a CSP.
7. Output: best idea, key risk, guardrail fit, not-advice reminder. Offer an order only if asked; show it in full and wait for an explicit yes.

# Trading Pearls (default guardrails)

On by default. During setup, show them and ask whether to keep or adjust. Save the final set as one guardrails memory. An override is the owner's call: note it and don't nag.

1. Own what you sell: quality, liquid names you'd hold, entries near support, about 5-10 names across sectors.
2. 30-45 DTE, 0.15-0.25 delta (0.20 or less preferred). Avoid weeklies.
3. Avoid carrying CSPs through earnings unless the owner chooses to.
4. Take profits at 30-50% with more than 30 DTE left, or ~70% inside 21 DTE.
5. At most one new entry per day. Doing nothing is fine.
6. Check positions 1-2 times a week. No emotional adds or revenge rolls.
7. Assignment is normal: covered calls at or above cost basis, sold into strength.
8. Keep cash above a floor the owner sets.
9. Broker data wins over spreadsheets and memory.
